sections.title: A Proposed Working Meeting
sections.content:
The note proposes a meeting at MIT Lincoln Laboratory on Friday, 8 May 1970, at 9:30 AM. A description of the Local Interaction Language (LIL) for the Terminal Support Processor (TSP) system will be presented.

The meeting is intended as a working group, and each host may send as many or as few interested people as it wishes.
sections.plainLanguage: The note invites interested people to a working meeting about LIL and the TSP system. It is an announcement of a planned meeting, not a report of its results.

sections.title: The TSP System and LIL
sections.content:
The TSP system is intended to provide flexible input and output for network users. The note says that users can program it in an interpretable language called LIL.

LIL includes primitives for manipulating tree structures for interactive graphics and for message-oriented input and output. Its general-purpose features specify input/output handlers and display structures.
sections.plainLanguage: The TSP system is meant to give network users flexible ways to send and receive information. LIL lets users describe input/output behavior and display structures, including tree structures for interactive graphics.

sections.title: Interactive Programs on the Network
sections.content:
The proposed meeting will include a discussion of problems in handling interactive programs over the ARPA Network. The note does not list specific solutions to those problems.

A working document on LIL is to be mailed to interested people about a week before the meeting.
sections.plainLanguage: The meeting will discuss the challenges of running interactive programs over the network. The announcement does not say what conclusions the group will reach.
